record: Branch protection's required status checks, read from GitHub.
read_at_revision_meaning: the tip of origin/main when the reading was taken
read_with: a local session holding GitHub credentials
cannot_verify: This file is a reading, not the protection itself. CI holds no GitHub credentials, so nothing in the test suite re-reads branch protection.

What the suite checks is that this file agrees with itself and with the tree: every required context is a name a workflow in this repository reports, every unprotected job is named here, the revision this reading was taken at is a commit this checkout still has, and the shard count is the workflow matrix's.

What it cannot check is the real protection on GitHub. A context added to branch protection after this reading, or removed from it, is invisible here until somebody re-reads it with credentials and rewrites this file.

The two shard-5 legs are named in the unprotected list because the reading of 2026-11-18 still does not find them in the required list. The owner has decided to add them; until that happens, the partition in .github/ci-shards.json keeps every test file in at least one leg this file names, so no test file waits for a leg a merge does not wait for.

This file names the legs, not what runs in them. The partition is .github/ci-shards.json, and the check that keeps every test file in a leg named here is `python .github/make_ci_shards.py --check`, which the lint job runs on every pull request.
